import pytest

from mdata.types import Prices
from risk.returns import log_returns

SAMPLE = Path(__file__).parents[2] / "contracts" / "mdata.Prices" / "sample.json"


def _sample_prices() -> Prices:
    data = json.loads(SAMPLE.read_text())
    return Prices(
        dates=tuple(data["dates"]),
        tickers=tuple(data["tickers"]),
        closes={t: tuple(c) for t, c in data["closes"].items()},
    )


def test_sample_dates_drop_the_first_as_base_date() -> None:
    result = log_returns(_sample_prices())
    assert result.base_date == "2024-01-02"
    assert result.dates == (
        "2024-01-03",
        "2024-01-04",
        "2024-01-05",
        "2024-01-08",
        "2024-01-09",
    )
    assert result.tickers == ("AAA", "BBB")


def test_sample_values_are_simple_returns() -> None:
    result = log_returns(_sample_prices())
    assert result.values["AAA"] == pytest.approx((0.01, -0.0148514851, 0.0251256281, 0.0147058824, -0.0067632850))
    assert result.values["BBB"][0] == pytest.approx(0.005)
    assert len(result.values["BBB"]) == 5


def test_two_dates_give_one_return() -> None:
    prices = Prices(dates=("d1", "d2"), tickers=("X",), closes={"X": (50.0, 40.0)})
    result = log_returns(prices)
    assert result.dates == ("d2",)
    assert result.values == {"X": pytest.approx((-0.2,))}


def test_fewer_than_two_dates_raises() -> None:
    prices = Prices(dates=("d1",), tickers=("X",), closes={"X": (50.0,)})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="two dates"):
        log_returns(prices)
